head: 9433cc6f3e21cffdb218b11b9da26ce70aa7889f
classification_reasons: Tight spec: spec.md's Flagged concerns is 'none'; the single open question carried from intent.md (how a non-integer dividend is rendered) is answered with a stated rationale (adopt the f-string/str() default, matching the intent's own stated default) rather than left open or silently decided; Acceptance gives exact, literal targets (str(exception) == "cannot divide 1 by zero"/"...1.5..."/"...1.0...", the full list of pre-existing tests that must keep passing, and the three healthy-output targets from CLAUDE.md).

Small blast radius: plan.md's 'Files that change' lists exactly two files (sample_pkg/calc.py, a new tests/test_messages.py); no .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml is touched in this diff; none of sdlc.yaml's risk_list items (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) apply to a one-line string change inside a pure arithmetic helper; no schema, migration or contract is touched; `percent` and `mean` and sample_pkg/__init__.py are verified unchanged.

Existing-test coverage: tests/test_calc.py::test_divide_by_zero_raises (confirmed present on HEAD, unchanged) already calls divide(1, 0) and asserts pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError) -- the exact branch and call this design modifies -- so the changed line is already exercised by a pre-existing test, not a brand-new, previously-unexercised code path.
attempted: Intent: read intent.md's Problem, Proposed outcome, Affected users/systems, Constraints and Open questions, and compared each bullet against spec.md's Requirements/Design/Acceptance and plan.md's Files/Order/Proof. Every bullet of the Proposed outcome and every Constraint is restated with the same substance (exact message text, exception type unchanged, percent's and mean's behaviour unchanged, new test file tests/test_messages.py, three green targets); nothing added or silently dropped. The one Open question (non-integer dividend formatting) is answered in spec.md's 'Open questions from intent' with a concrete rationale instead of being carried forward unresolved.

Spec and plan: read spec.md and plan.md end to end against each other and against intent.md. plan.md's 'Files that change' order (calc.py, then tests/test_messages.py) matches its own 'Order of work' order; 'Risks' names the riskiest step (a typo swapping `a` for `b` in the f-string) and checks for message-matching callers (none found in-repo); 'Options not taken' records three rejected designs (repr() instead of str(), touching percent, adding non-integer-formatting tests) with reasons tied back to intent.md and spec.md; 'Proof' lists only named tests plus the three CLAUDE.md targets, flagging which is still to be written. spec.md's per-skill rows (ux-conventions, data-conventions, security-baseline) are reasoned, not asserted blankly.

Proof: this is phase (b), design-only; diff-b.patch touches only intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml and this change's own evidence/* -- no sample_pkg/*.py or tests/*.py yet, correct for this phase (confirmed tests/test_messages.py does not exist on disk yet). Read sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py and tests/test_calc.py directly at HEAD to check the design's premises: divide's current raise is exactly `raise ZeroDivisionError("b must not be zero")` on `b == 0` (line 10); percent catches ZeroDivisionError and re-raises its own literal message via `raise ... from None` (lines 17-18), so it never surfaces divide's text regardless of what divide's message says; mean only reaches divide after its own non-empty check, so len(values) is never zero on that call. All three premises hold, matching spec.md's Design section word for word.

Blast radius: confirmed via the diff's own paths that nothing outside changes/0016-name-the-dividend-in-divide-s-error/** changes in this phase; no guardrail file in the diff; sdlc.yaml's risk_list (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) does not apply; CLAUDE.md's Layout section already documents tests/test_messages.py as 'checks the error messages' (added in PR #76), so the plan's claim that no Layout update is needed is verified true, not just asserted (CLAUDE.md's own 'Things Claude gets wrong' entry about stale Layout entries is correctly addressed).

Policies: compared spec.md's per-skill reasoning against coding-standards/SKILL.md (read directly): rule 4 ('every behavior change ships with a test that fails without it') is satisfied by the planned tests/test_messages.py test, which cannot pass against the current code (today's message is 'b must not be zero'). ux-conventions and data-conventions are correctly marked not applicable (library exception text, no schema/storage/migration touched, and the message only echoes a value the caller already supplied). security-baseline is correctly reduced to 'no new dependency, no endpoint, no secret, no external input' given no risk_list hit.

Tests: no pre-existing test is weakened, skipped or deleted anywhere in this diff (the diff touches no test file at all, since it's design-only); plan.md explicitly keeps tests/test_calc.py and tests/test_flag.py untouched, matching intent.md's Constraints. The planned new test asserts a literal string that is false against current code, so it is not vacuous.
Skip markers: none appear anywhere in this diff (design-only phase, no test or source file touched yet); plan.md declares none, correctly, since the ratchets check runs at phases (c)/(d), not (b).

Noted but not used as an escalation reason: status.yaml classifies this change_type: feature, while the structurally identical prior change 0015 (name the zero whole in percent's error, also a message-only correction with no new public function) was classified change_type: fix and followed an explicit test-first order of work under build guide step 25. 0016's plan.md instead implements before writing the test. Checked coding-standards/SKILL.md directly: rule 4 only requires the test to exist and fail without the fix, not a specific commit order, and the test-first/test-lock discipline in sdlc.yaml applies only to fix-type changes -- so, as classified, plan.md's order does not breach a stated rule. This is left as an observation, not a reason, because I could not find a rule it actually violates given the change_type as set.

Not used as a reason: no deterministic gate/skill check (gate/cli.py check, any skill's check.py) was run or cited; the reasons above rest on reading intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, sdlc.yaml, REVIEW.md, CLAUDE.md, sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py and tests/test_calc.py directly, plus the prior change 0015 as a precedent for calibrating the routine/non-routine line.
